doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: Being a realist; what makes her angry
summary: She calls herself a realist, dislikes BS and abuse, and credits her mother's belief in equal rights.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: I say I’m a realist. I don’t know about optimist. You know I don’t think things are great or bad I just think they are what they are. And what are you going to do about it you know. You do the best you can do within the circumstances. And I try to just be a nice person and treat other people well and hope to be around people that feel that way or whatever. You know. And I like to feel good. I like to have fun you know, in the midst of everything that’s going on around us. Because you know I think the world’s always been a mess. So it is what it is.
Anything in particular that makes you angry? Either musically or —

I don’t like to get angry. That’s not a nice — I don’t like that emotion. But B.S. makes me angry. Somebody posing as something but they’re not really that, or saying you’re going to do something that you have no intention of doing, so that type of thing. Or verbal abuse. Just abuse. You know people just trying to get over on one another. I don’t like that. My mother didn’t like that. My mother was a big advocate of equal, you know, equal rights, equal pay, equal treatment of people. So that’s how I grew up. So I like clear communication and taking responsibility for one’s actions.
